baseline: Before starting: FBC, renal and liver profile, urea/BUN, urinary protein, blood glucose, cholesterol and triglycerides. Confirm the endocrine indication, review lung symptoms and infections, and check all medicines. Assess bone/fracture risk for the exemestane component.
ongoing: FBC, renal/liver profile, cholesterol and triglycerides every four weeks or as clinically indicated. Check fasting glucose as clinically indicated, with closer monitoring if diabetes or another medicine increases risk. Ask about mouth soreness, infection, cough/breathlessness and daily function at reviews.
component_rule: If everolimus is interrupted or reduced for toxicity, NCCP says exemestane may continue; the treating team must confirm the plan for each medicine. Do not stop both automatically or restart everolimus yourself. Everolimus can increase toxicity around radiotherapy and impair wound healing: agree a specific plan before radiotherapy or surgery.
key_audit_findings: NCCP 00322 is not an exemestane monotherapy card and not an adjuvant endocrine regimen; do not inherit those eligibility lists.
The old encoding had only two generic rules and no operative ANC/platelet or detailed toxicity decisions. This audit adds 77 source-linked rules with component-specific actions.
NCCP Table 3 uses CTCAE v3.0. Do not infer its metabolic/stomatitis grade solely from a generic CTCAE v5 label.
For grade 3 febrile neutropenia, the NCCP restart ANC is ≥1.25×10^9/L with no fever, different from the afebrile neutropenia threshold ≥1.
Exemestane continues through everolimus interruption or modification unless a separate clinical reason changes the plan.
Child-Pugh A/B/C: NCCP everolimus 75%/50%/25% of original dose. EU SmPC adds benefit-risk qualification and 2.5 mg/day maximum for Child-Pugh C. No automatic combined hepatic/toxicity restart dose.
No automatic imaging schedule is invented. The clinical team must define the response-assessment plan; pulmonary symptoms warrant urgent investigation.
Radiotherapy is not a routine phase of this regimen. Show any actual radiotherapy on a parallel individual plan, with an explicit joint decision about everolimus timing.

evidence.title: BOLERO-2 final progression-free survival analysis
evidence.population: 724 postmenopausal patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer after non-steroidal aromatase inhibitors; everolimus+exemestane versus placebo+exemestane.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Investigator-assessed PFS: median 7.8 versus 3.2 months; HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.38–0.54), p<0.0001. Central review: 11.0 versus 4.1 months.
evidence.interpretation: Adding mTOR inhibition delayed progression compared with exemestane alone in this trial population.
evidence.limitations: Conducted before routine CDK4/6-inhibitor use; the observed benefit is not a guaranteed individual outcome and is not direct randomised evidence for current post-CDK4/6 sequencing.

evidence.title: BOLERO-2 overall survival analysis
evidence.population: Same randomised BOLERO-2 population; overall survival was a key secondary endpoint.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Overall survival: median 31.0 versus 26.6 months; HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.73–1.10), p=0.14.
evidence.interpretation: No statistically significant overall-survival advantage was demonstrated. Do not present the PFS benefit as proven longer survival.
evidence.limitations: Subsequent therapies were common; OS was secondary, and the confidence interval includes no difference.

evidence.title: SWISH stomatitis-prevention study
evidence.population: Single-arm prevention study in 92 postmenopausal women starting everolimus+exemestane; 85 evaluable for the week 8 stomatitis endpoint in the EU SmPC report.
evidence.primary_endpoint: EU SmPC reports Grade ≥2 stomatitis at 8 weeks in 2/85 (2.4%); no Grade 3/4 cases.
evidence.interpretation: Supports discussing a prescribed alcohol-free dexamethasone mouthwash early in treatment. Study regimen: 0.5 mg/5 mL solution, 10 mL swished for 2 minutes and spat four times daily for 8 weeks; local formulation/prescribing review is needed.
evidence.limitations: Single-arm study with historical comparison, not a randomised concurrent control; oral candidiasis occurred and the mouthwash is a separate prescription.
